answers.answer: Reveal a region card for the King; each player takes another region card as their home and puts their Grande there. Each starts with ten Caballeros: two beside the Grande in the home region, one on the first success-track space, and seven in court.
answers.evidence: Setup: reveal the top region card and put the King there; each player's other region card determines home. Initial ten are two home, one on track, seven in court.

answers.answer: Players choose the round-1 starter. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round leads; others play clockwise. No power-card value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: players choose who begins in round 1; later the player who took the last turn begins; others play clockwise; no value already played may be matched.

answers.answer: Turns are taken in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the Caballero allowance shown on your power card from the provinces into your court; recruiting fewer is allowed. Recruitment happens before choosing an action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'At the start of your turn recruit up to' the pictured number; after recruitment, choose an available action card.

answers.answer: If your provinces do not have enough of your Caballeros, you may take your own from the board to make up the difference. The King's region and Castillo cannot supply pieces for recruitment.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: 'you may take your own from the board to make up the difference'; King's region remains taboo and Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment is from your court to regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo, and the allowance may be divided freely among those destinations. The action-card number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none.
answers.evidence: Actions: deployment from court to any regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or Castillo, dividing allowance freely; number is a maximum.

answers.answer: Yes. Complete ordinary deployment and the special action in either order, but complete one activity before starting the other; neither can be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: do them 'in either order' but complete one before the other; 'You may decline the special action.'

answers.answer: After a player's turn, their selected action card is laid aside and unavailable to later players. At the end of the round, discard the remaining face-up cards. The King card is revealed again each round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: lay aside selected card; discard remaining face-up cards after all turns; King card is revealed again every round and never permanently discarded.

answers.answer: Caballeros, Grandes, and mobile scoreboards may not move into or out of the King's region, but it can still be scored. An action that moves the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: no Caballero, Grande or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of it; it may still be scored. Actions that move the King change the protected region.

answers.answer: Announce clearly how many Caballeros enter the Castillo. Entry is allowed regardless of the King's location. They leave only during general scoring; no action removes them from the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Actions: announce clearly how many go inside; Caballeros may enter regardless of King's location; they leave only during general scoring.

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. First, before uncovering the Castillo, each player secretly chooses one permitted board-region destination for all their Castillo Caballeros (not the King's region). Second, uncover and score the Castillo. Third, reveal disks and move every player's Castillo pieces to their chosen region; if the King's region was illegally chosen, those pieces go to that player's court. Replace the empty Castillo. Fourth, score the nine regions in scoring-track order and record points.
answers.evidence: General scoring: 'Secretly select destinations before uncovering'; score Castillo; reveal disks and empty it; score nine regions. Timing after 3, 6, 9.

answers.answer: A player must send all their Castillo Caballeros to one region, so they cannot split them or retain any in the Castillo. They may not choose the King's region. If they illegally chose it, those pieces go to their court instead; that does not make it a legal choice.
answers.evidence: General scoring: all a player's Castillo Caballeros go to one region; choosing King's region is prohibited; none may be retained or split; illegal selection sends pieces to court.

answers.answer: They score 3, 3, 3, and 1 respectively. Grandes do not count toward majority; only Caballeros count.
answers.evidence: Publisher example on 5/3/1 with counts 4,4,4,3 scores 3,3,3,1; only Caballeros count and Grande contributes zero.

answers.answer: The players with 4, 3, and 2 Caballeros score 6, 4, and 0; the other player with 2 also scores 0.
answers.evidence: Publisher example on 6/4/2 with counts 4,3,2,2 scores 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: In a two-player game, only first place can pay; in a three-player game, first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first shifts to second place, which is outside the payable ranks, so both score zero.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: two players only first pays; three players first and second; apply cutoff after tie shift, so a two-player tie for first pays neither.

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scorings, the sole majority holder gets +2 for the King's bonus in the King's region and +2 for the home bonus if their own Grande is there. Neither bonus is awarded on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses apply whenever a region is scored, including special scorings; each is +2 for sole majority; neither on a tie for first.

answers.answer: No. Special Castillo scoring uncovers and scores its contents, then covers the same Caballeros again. It neither empties nor redistributes them.
answers.evidence: Special scoring of Castillo: reveal and score its contents, then cover the same pieces again without redistribution.

answers.answer: A scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo. It may not move into or out of the King's region. The two scoreboards cannot be stacked. Keep them right side up as 8/4/0 or 4/0/0; do not rotate them to invent values.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: scoreboard can be introduced or moved; Castillo allowed; no movement into/out of King's region; cannot stack; place right side up, never reversed or rotated.

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region, but not into the King's region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King's region. Other Grandes may already be at the destination. The destination becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Grande: move to another region except King's region or Castillo; cannot leave King's region; destination may contain several Grandes; destination becomes new home.

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the one played that turn. You need not reveal which card; if it is the visible top card, taking it will of course be apparent.
answers.evidence: Power Cards: return any one played card, including this turn's; need not reveal which, though taking visible top card is apparent.

answers.answer: The standard game ends after all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins; no additional tiebreaker is given.
answers.evidence: End: finish all stages of third general scoring after round 9; furthest along success track wins; no additional tiebreaker.

answers.answer: Separate action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place face down. Reveal the top card of each of the five stacks at the start of each round. The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup: separate into stacks 1–5, shuffle separately, face down. Turn Structure reveals top card of each five stacks; standard marker starts at 1.

answers.answer: No, played power cards remain in the player's face-up used stack rather than returning to hand. Only the top card is visible.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: played cards remain in each player's face-up used stack with only the top card visible.

answers.answer: Use the King's new position if the King card special action is done before ordinary deployment; otherwise deployment uses his old position. The King may be placed in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: King card: put King in any region except Castillo; use current location at time of ordinary deployment. Protected locations section clarifies old/new position by order.

answers.answer: Put the Veto card before you and retain it to stop one special action during this round or the next. It cannot stop the ordinary deployment part of another action card.
answers.evidence: Veto: put card before you and retain to stop one special action during this round or next; cannot stop ordinary deployment.

answers.answer: Yes. While a Veto is held, other players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: you can stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete action. A completed action cannot be vetoed; already executed parts are not undone, though you may prevent just part.
answers.evidence: Veto: must announce; object as soon as action starts; stop before execution or remaining incomplete part; completed actions cannot be vetoed; executed parts are not undone.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Veto: discard after using once; if unused, discard at end of next round.

answers.answer: Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; the selecting player is unaffected. A player with an empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros to provinces; empty court sends none; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player sends all two Caballeros they have, since fewer than three. You, the selecting player, are unaffected and keep your five in court.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority — three from court: each fellow player sends three, or all they have if fewer; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed execution paragraph and card face say each player, including the selecting player, sends three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Start with the player to the selecting player's left, proceed clockwise, and have the selecting player go last. Pieces may come from any regions and/or court, but not the King's region or Castillo. The source gives no explicit rule if someone has fewer than three eligible pieces. The bold heading instead says 'fellow players.'
answers.evidence: The King returns: detailed paragraph and card say each player including selector sends three; left then clockwise, selector last; sources any regions/court except King's region/Castillo; heading says 'fellow players'; no shortfall rule.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each to its owner's provinces. No pieces may be taken from courts, the King's region, or the Castillo. The source gives no fallback if a player has no eligible piece.
answers.evidence: Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one from a region for each player including themselves; no court, King's region or Castillo; no explicit fallback.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses one region on their disk, simultaneously; choices are revealed together. The chosen region must contain at least two of that player's Caballeros, and two are returned to provinces. A player with a legal region containing at least two must choose such a region. Never take from the King's region or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove two: each affected player secretly chooses one region, simultaneous reveal; it must contain at least two; return two; protected sources excluded.

answers.answer: If they have at most one Caballero in every region, they choose a region with one and return that one to the provinces. The summary does not verify a fallback for different configurations such as two or more protected pieces with only singletons elsewhere.
answers.evidence: The stated singleton fallback applies if the player has at most one in every region: choose a region with one and return it; other fallback is not verified.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects a region containing at least one of their Caballeros; all choices are revealed together, and each returns all their own pieces there to the provinces. A player with no Caballeros in any region is unaffected. The King's region and Castillo are excluded.
answers.evidence: Fellow players secretly remove all from one region: simultaneous secret selection, region with at least one own Caballero, return all own there; none in any region is unaffected; taboo sources excluded.

answers.answer: Yes, the player may choose any region, including the King's region or Castillo. Use normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits, and bonuses. If Castillo is chosen, score it and cover the same pieces again; do not redistribute them.
answers.evidence: Pick one region to score: any region including King's region or Castillo; normal rules and bonuses; Castillo pieces covered again, not distributed.

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia 4/2/0, Catalonia 4/2/1, and Seville 4/3/1. Eligibility uses the current first value, with mobile scoreboards replacing printed values. Thus Galicia with 8/4/0 does not qualify, while Granada with 4/0/0 does. Applicable bonuses apply to special scoring.
answers.evidence: All 4-value regions table names printed group; mobile scoreboard replaces printed values for category eligibility; examples say mobile 8/4/0 removes Galicia and 4/0/0 adds Granada; bonuses apply to special scorings.

answers.answer: The printed 5-value group is Basque Country 5/3/1, Aragon 5/4/1, Valencia 5/3/2. The printed 6-and-7 group is Old Castile 6/4/2, New Castile 7/4/2, Granada 6/3/1. Current first values under mobile scoreboards determine group eligibility. Castillo is not scored in all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Special scoring table lists these printed groups; mobile scoreboard replaces printed values for points and eligibility; all-5 explicitly excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Only sole first places score; tied leaders receive nothing because a tie for first would ordinarily receive second-place value. Lower ranks also score nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: First position only: only sole first places score; tie for first scores nothing; other ranks get nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Both board regions tied for the most are scored. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored, even if it contains more Caballeros than either region.
answers.evidence: Most-Caballeros card scores all board regions tied for most; Castillo is neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions, score every region tied for the least, and ignore empty regions. The Castillo is neither considered nor scored.
answers.evidence: Least-Caballeros card compares nonempty board regions, scores all tied for least; empty regions and Castillo are not considered or scored.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each secretly chooses another region on their disk; choices are revealed simultaneously, and each player's group moves to that destination. If a player chooses the King's region or the region being vacated, their pieces go to their court instead. The King's taboo bars taking pieces out of the King's region, and this card cannot empty the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Movement: fellow players move all own pieces out; destinations secretly chosen and revealed simultaneously; choosing King's region or vacated region sends pieces to court; taboo bars King's region source; Castillo cannot be emptied.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King to a neighboring region, no more than one region away. The King card allows placing him in any region except Castillo.
answers.evidence: Royal Adviser: neighboring region, no more than one away. King card: any region except Castillo; summary says wider choice.

answers.answer: The Court adds two of your own Caballeros from the provinces to your court. This special action is separate from the 4-stack card's ordinary deployment of up to four from court to the board; either complete activity may go first. The source gives no explicit shortfall procedure if provinces cannot supply two.
answers.evidence: The Court: move two own Caballeros from provinces to court; separate from ordinary up-to-four deployment; activities may go first; no explicit shortfall procedure.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose on their disks and reveal simultaneously. The disk allows any of the nine board regions, including the King's region, but not Castillo. Score each uniquely chosen region under normal rules; a region selected by multiple players is not scored.
answers.evidence: Each secretly chooses a region to score: choices secret and simultaneous; King's region allowed, Castillo not; unique selections score; duplicates do not.

answers.answer: You may take all your own Caballeros from one region and distribute them among other regions and/or the Castillo; you may return some to the original region. Origins exclude the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region but can include Castillo. Ordinary deployment remains separately subject to adjacency.
answers.evidence: Intrigue all-own-from-one-region: distribute among other regions and/or Castillo; may return some to original; origins exclude King's region/Castillo; destinations exclude King's region but may include Castillo.

answers.answer: Up to three may enter the board in total: the normal deployment of up to one plus up to two additional Caballeros from court. Only the normal one requires adjacency; the two additional ones may go to any non-King region and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue two more from court: up to two additional to any non-King regions/Castillo; with normal one, up to three enter, only normal one requires adjacency.

answers.answer: No. Choose one special alternative: either up to two additional Caballeros from court or all your own Caballeros from one region. The normal up-to-one deployment still applies.
answers.evidence: Intrigue choice: choose one preceding special action, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: The maximum is five Caballeros, and they may be own and/or foreign, but all must come from one origin region. They go to other non-King regions and/or Castillo; they cannot come from multiple origins.
answers.evidence: Intrigue up-to-five effect: own and/or foreign from one origin region, distributed to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move up to three foreign Caballeros only; your own pieces cannot be included. They may come from multiple non-King board regions, never from Castillo, and may go to any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any-three-foreign: up to three other players' pieces from any non-King board regions including multiple origins, never Castillo; destinations any non-King regions/Castillo.

answers.answer: The any-three card allows up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions, with multiple origins allowed, to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. The any-four card allows up to four own and/or foreign Caballeros from any non-King origin regions, but destinations must be other non-King regions and/or Castillo, preserving its 'other regions' wording.
answers.evidence: Intrigue table: any three from any non-King origins to any non-King destinations; any four from any non-King origins into other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros, as separate ownership allowances. Multiple origins are allowed. Sources may be any non-King board regions, never the Castillo; destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue two-own-and-two-foreign: separate allowances; multiple origins allowed; never take from Castillo; move to any non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: Move up to four Caballeros, own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Intrigue any-four-own: up to four own only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: On the 4-stack secret-choice scoring card, the disk permits the King's region but not the Castillo; unique choices score and duplicates do not. This differs from the card where its player picks any one region: that card permits both the King's region and Castillo, and Castillo scoring leaves the pieces covered in place.
answers.evidence: 4-stack secret scoring: nine board regions including King's region, not Castillo. Pick-one scoring allows King's region or Castillo; Castillo pieces are covered again.

answers.answer: The mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. On the special action, you may either introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Setup places both mobile scoreboards beside board; Stack 4 action allows introducing one from beside the board or moving one already on it.

answers.answer: Each player receives thirteen power cards in their own color, with values 1 through 13.
answers.evidence: Components/setup: each player gets their color's thirteen power cards; component description says values 1–13 per color.
